tagline: Offline optical data exchange · screen → camera
summary: PR #5 is merged and the project dashboard is live. Discovery has now confirmed substantial public prior art, ranked the first target scenarios, and drafted a reproducible benchmark protocol. G1 remains intentionally unapproved until scenario evidence and the physical-test baseline are reviewed.

pullRequest.title: Sprint 0 discovery: scenario scoring, benchmark spec and competitive landscape

currentFocus.title: Validate the top 5 product scenarios
currentFocus.detail: The first scoring pass favors OEM optical service/export, industrial HMI diagnostics, managed isolated-workstation export, field-service exchange, and GMP read-only export. The next step is stronger buyer/workflow evidence.

currentFocus.title: Finalize the benchmark protocol before code
currentFocus.detail: A draft now defines incompressible payloads, repeated runs, SHA-256 correctness, net-goodput timing, environment capture and the ≥100 KB/s G0 success rule. Baseline hardware/conditions still require G1 review.

currentFocus.title: Turn prior art into product differentiation
currentFocus.detail: Public projects already demonstrate animated-code optical transfer at useful speeds. OptiLink must decide whether its moat is enterprise/industrial governance, OEM integration and structured data exchange rather than raw file transfer.

approvals.title: First MVP hypothesis
approvals.decision: Computer → Android; screen-to-camera; one-way offline file transfer; browser sender preferred; ≥100 KB/s net-goodput validation target.

approvals.title: Initial technical and product path
approvals.decision: Before approval: review top scenarios, prior-art/licensing implications, product positioning, benchmark device/conditions, sender/receiver baseline, carrier and one-way loss-recovery strategy.
